layout.header: Tamsin Hollow Breweries Limited | Board resolutions

new: Written Resolutions of the Board
Tamsin Hollow Breweries Limited (company number 07654321)

The following resolutions were passed as written resolutions of the directors of the Company on 17 April 2025 in accordance with the articles of association of the Company and section 248 of the Companies Act 2006.
Directors
Director
Role
Date signed
Edmund Rourke
Chair
17 April 2025
Hana Okafor
Finance director
17 April 2025
Lewis Penhaligon
Non-executive director
18 April 2025
Background
The directors noted that the Company proposes to acquire a new bottling line from Severn Process Equipment Ltd for a price of £640,000, to be financed in part by a term loan from Dunmore Bank plc.
Resolutions
Approval of the acquisition
It was resolved that the acquisition of the bottling line on the terms of the draft purchase agreement presented to the directors be approved.
It was resolved that any one director be authorised to sign the purchase agreement on behalf of the Company, with such amendments as that director considers appropriate.
Approval of the facility
It was resolved that the Company enter into a term loan facility of up to £400,000 with Dunmore Bank plc, repayable over 5 years.
It was resolved that the Company grant a debenture in favour of Dunmore Bank plc as security for the facility.
It was resolved that the finance director be authorised to deliver any utilisation request under the facility.
Declarations of interest

Lewis Penhaligon declared that he is a shareholder in Severn Process Equipment Ltd, and the other directors resolved that he can nevertheless count in the quorum and vote on these resolutions, as permitted by the articles of association.
Filings
It was resolved that the company secretary be instructed to:
register the debenture at Companies House within 21 days of its creation; and
update the Company's statutory registers accordingly.
Signatures
Signed by each director to signify agreement to the resolutions above.

new: Written Resolutions of the Board
Tamsin Hollow Breweries Limited (company number 07654321)

The following resolutions were passed as written resolutions of the directors of the Company on 17 April 2025 in accordance with the articles of association of the Company and section 248 of the Companies Act 2006.
Directors
Director
Role
Date signed
Edmund Rourke
Chair
17 April 2025
Hana Okafor
Finance director
17 April 2025
Lewis Penhaligon
Non-executive director
18 April 2025
Background
The directors noted that the Company proposes to acquire a new bottling line from Severn Process Equipment Ltd for a price of £640,000, to be financed in part by a term loan from Dunmore Bank plc.
Resolutions
Approval of the acquisition
It was resolved that the acquisition of the bottling line terms of the draft purchase agreement presented to the directors without undue delay be approved.
It was resolved that any one director be authorised to sign the purchase agreement on behalf of the Company, with such amendments as that director considers appropriate.
Approval of the facility
It was to the extent permitted by law resolved that the Company enter into a term loan facility of up to £400,000 with Dunmore Bank plc, repayable over 6 years.
It was resolved that the Company grant a debenture in favour of Dunmore Bank plc as security for the facility.
It was resolved that the finance director be authorised to deliver any utilisation request under the facility.
Declarations of interest

Lewis Penhaligon declared that he is a shareholder in Severn Process Equipment Ltd, and the other directors resolved that he may nevertheless count in the quorum and vote on these resolutions, as permitted by the articles of association.
Filings
It was resolved that the company secretary be instructed to:
register the debenture at Companies House within 21 days of its creation; and
update the Company's statutory registers accordingly.
Signatures
Signed by each director to signify agreement to the resolutions above.

new: Lease of Unit 7, Fernhill Trading Estate
Particulars and Terms
This Lease is made on 1 October 2025 between Fernhill Estates Limited (the "Landlord") and Quillon Print Works Ltd (the "Tenant").
Particulars
Item
Detail
Property
Unit 7, Fernhill Trading Estate, together with the rights set out in Schedule 1
Term
10 years from and including the Term Commencement Date
Initial annual rent
Rent deposit
Letting and rent
The Landlord lets the Property to the Tenant for the term set out in the Particulars.
The Tenant shall pay the annual rent by unequal quarterly payments in advance on the usual quarter days.
The rent shall be reviewed on the fifth anniversary of the Term Commencement Date to the higher of the rent then payable and the open market rent.
The Tenant shall pay a service charge equal to a fair proportion of the costs reasonably incurred by the Landlord in providing the Services to the Estate.
Tenant covenants
Repair and alterations
The Tenant shall keep the Property in good and substantial repair and condition, except for damage caused by an Insured Risk.
The Tenant shall not make any structural alterations to the Property, and shall not make any other alterations without the consent of the Landlord, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld.
Use and dealings
The Tenant shall use the Property only for purposes within Class B2 or Class B8 of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987.
The Tenant shall not:
assign the whole of the Property without the consent of the Landlord;
assign or underlet part only of the Property; or
share occupation of the Property with any person other than a group company.
Insurance
The Landlord shall insure the Property against the Insured Risks for its full reinstatement cost, and the Tenant shall pay the Landlord on demand the insurance rent.
If the Property is damaged by an Insured Risk so as to be unfit for use, the rent shall be suspended until the Property is fit for use or for 3 years, whichever is shorter.
Break and re-entry
The Tenant may terminate this Lease on the fifth anniversary of the Term Commencement Date by giving the Landlord not less than 6 months' written notice, provided that it has paid all rent due.
The Landlord may re-enter the Property if any rent is unpaid for 21 days after becoming payable, or if the Tenant breaches any covenant in this Lease, and clause 5.1 shall not apply after re-entry.
Deposit and law
The Tenant shall provide the rent deposit, to be held by the Landlord in a designated account and returned within 28 days after the end of the Term.
This Lease is governed by the law of England and Wales.
Signatures
Executed as a deed by Fernhill Estates Limited acting by [NAME], a director, in the presence of a witness.
Executed as a deed by Quillon Print Works Ltd acting by [NAME], a director, in the presence of a witness.

This Lease is made on 1 October 2025 between Fernhill Estates Limited (the "Landlord") and Quillon Print Works Ltd (the "Tenant").
Particulars
Item
Detail
Property
Unit 7, Fernhill Trading Estate, together with the rights set out in Schedule 1
Term
10 years from and including the Term Commencement Date
Initial annual rent
Rent deposit
Letting and rent
The Landlord lets the Property to the Tenant for the term set out in the Particulars.
The Tenant shall pay the annual rent by equal quarterly payments in advance on the usual quarter days.
The rent shall be reviewed on the fifth anniversary of the Term Commencement Date to the higher of the rent then payable and the open market rent.
The Tenant shall pay a service charge equal to a fair proportion of the costs reasonably incurred by the Landlord in providing the Services to the Estate.
Tenant covenants
Repair and alterations
The Tenant shall keep the Property in good and substantial repair and condition, except for damage caused by an Insured Risk.
The Tenant shall not make any structural alterations to the Property, and shall not make any other alterations without the consent of the Landlord, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld.
Use and dealings
The Tenant shall use the Property only for purposes within Class B2 or Class B8 of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987.
The Tenant shall not:
assign the whole of the Property without the consent of the Landlord;
assign or underlet part only of the Property; or
share occupation of the Property with any person other than a group company.
Insurance
The Landlord shall insure the Property against the Insured Risks for its full reinstatement cost, and the Tenant shall pay the Landlord on demand the insurance rent.
If the Property is damaged by an Insured Risk so as to be unfit for use, the rent shall be suspended until the Property is fit for use or for 3 years, whichever is shorter.
Break and re-entry
The Tenant may terminate this Lease on the fifth anniversary of the Term Commencement Date by giving the Landlord not less than 6 months' written notice, provided that it has paid all rent due.
The Landlord may re-enter the Property if any rent is unpaid for 21 days after becoming payable, or if the Tenant breaches any covenant in this Lease, and clause 5.1 shall not apply after re-entry.
Deposit and law
The Tenant shall provide the rent deposit, to be held by the Landlord in a designated account and returned within 28 days after the end of the Term.
This Lease is governed by the law of England and Wales.
Signatures
Executed as a deed by Fernhill Estates Limited acting by [NAME], a director, in the presence of a witness.
Executed as a deed by Quillon Print Works Ltd acting by [NAME], a director, in the presence of a witness.

Particulars and Terms
This Lease is made on 1 October 2025 between Fernhill Estates Limited (the "Landlord") and Quillon Print Works Ltd (the "Tenant").
Particulars
Item
Detail
Property
Unit 7, Fernhill Trading Estate, together with the rights set out in Schedule 1
Break date
the fifth anniversary of the Term Commencement Date
Term
10 years from and including the Term Commencement Date
Initial annual rent
Rent deposit
Letting and rent
The Tenant shall pay the annual rent by equal quarterly payments in advance on the usual quarter days.
The rent shall be reviewed on the fifth anniversary of the Term Commencement Date to the higher of the rent then payable and the open market rent.
The Tenant shall pay a service charge equal to a fair proportion of the costs reasonably incurred by the Landlord in providing the Services to the Estate.
Tenant covenants
Repair and alterations
The Tenant shall keep the Property in good and substantial repair and condition, except for damage caused by an Insured Risk.
The Tenant shall not make any structural alterations to the Property, and shall not make any other alterations without the consent of the Landlord, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld.
Use and dealings
The Tenant shall use the Property only for purposes within Class B2 or Class B8 of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987.
No failure or delay by a party in exercising any right or remedy shall operate as a waiver of that right or remedy, nor shall it prevent any further exercise of it.
assign the whole of the Property without the consent of the Landlord;
assign or underlet part only of the Property; or
Any notice under this Agreement shall be in writing and delivered by hand, by pre-paid first class post or by email to the address of the recipient set out above.
Insurance
The Landlord shall insure the Property against the Insured Risks for its full reinstatement cost, and the Tenant shall pay the Landlord on demand the insurance rent.
If the Property is damaged by an Insured Risk so as to be unfit for use, the rent shall be suspended until the Property is fit for use or for 3 years, whichever is shorter.
This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one agreement.

new: Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement
Harbourline Analytics Limited and Copperfield Robotics Ltd
This Agreement is made on 3 March 2025 between the parties set out in the table below.
Party
Company number
Registered office
Harbourline Analytics Limited ("Harbourline")
14 Canal Street, Manchester M1 3HE
Copperfield Robotics Ltd ("Copperfield")
2 Harbour Road, Leith EH6 6LX
Background
Each party wishes to disclose certain Confidential Information to the other for the purpose of evaluating a possible joint development of warehouse automation software (the "Purpose").
Definitions
"Confidential Information" means all information of a confidential nature disclosed by one party to the other, whether in writing, orally or by any other means, including:
technical data, source code and designs;
customer lists, pricing and business plans; and
any information marked as confidential, whether or not it would otherwise be confidential.

Confidential Information does not include information that is or becomes generally available to the public other than through a breach of this Agreement, or that the receiving party can show was lawfully in its possession before disclosure.
Obligations
The receiving party shall keep the Confidential Information secret and shall not use it for any purpose other than the Purpose.

The receiving party may disclose Confidential Information to its employees, officers and professional advisers who need to know it for the Purpose, provided that it ensures each of them is bound by obligations of confidence no less strict than those in this Agreement.

The receiving party may disclose Confidential Information to the extent required by law, by any court of competent jurisdiction or by any regulatory body, provided that it gives the disclosing party as much notice of the disclosure as is lawful and practicable.

On the written request of the disclosing party, the receiving party must within 10 Business Days return or destroy all documents containing Confidential Information and certify in writing that it has done so, save that it may keep one copy to comply with clause 3.3.
General
Nothing in this Agreement grants the receiving party any licence or other right in the Confidential Information, which remains the property of the disclosing party.
All Confidential Information is provided as is, and neither party gives any warranty as to its accuracy or completeness.
The obligations in this Agreement continue for a period of 3 years from the date of this Agreement, regardless of whether the parties enter into any further agreement.
Damages alone may not be an adequate remedy for a breach of this Agreement, and the disclosing party is entitled to seek an injunction or other equitable relief for any threatened or actual breach.
Notices under this Agreement shall be sent to legal@harbourline.example.com for Harbourline and to contracts@copperfield.example.com for Copperfield.
This Agreement and any dispute arising out of it are governed by the law of England and Wales, and the courts of England have exclusive jurisdiction.
Signatures
Signed for and on behalf of Harbourline Analytics Limited by [NAME], director.
Signed for and on behalf of Copperfield Robotics Ltd by [NAME], director.

new: Software Subscription Terms
Brightwater Scheduling platform
These Terms apply to the subscription by the Customer to the Brightwater Scheduling platform supplied by Brightwater Systems Limited (the "Supplier").
Licence

The Supplier grants the Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable right during the Subscription Term to permit the Authorised Users to use the Platform solely for the Customer's internal business operations.
The Customer shall not permit more than the number of Authorised Users stated in the Order Form to access the Platform at every time.
The Customer shall not:
copy, modify or create derivative works of the Platform;
reverse engineer or decompile the Platform, except to the extent expressly permitted by the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988; or
use the Platform to provide services to third parties.
Service levels
The Supplier shall use commercially reasonable endeavours to make the Platform available 99.5% of the time in each calendar month, excluding planned maintenance notified at least 48 hours in advance.
The Supplier shall respond to and resolve incidents within the times in the table below, measured in Business Hours.
Priority
Response time
Target resolution
Priority 1
1 hour
4 hours
Priority 2
4 hours
2 Business Days
Priority 3
1 Business Day
10 Business Days
Support requests shall be sent to support@brightwater.example.com.
Customer Data
The Customer owns all Customer Data and grants the Supplier a licence to use it only to the extent necessary to provide the Platform and the support services.

The Supplier shall process personal data on behalf of the Customer only on the Customer's documented instructions and in accordance with the data processing terms in Schedule 2, which apply mutatis mutandis to any sub-processor.
The Supplier shall back up Customer Data daily and retain each backup for 30 days.
Fees and term
The Customer shall pay the Subscription Fees annually in advance, and the Supplier may increase the Subscription Fees on each anniversary of the Start Date by not more than 5%.

The Subscription Term starts on the Start Date and continues for an initial period of 24 months, after which it renews automatically for successive periods of 12 months unless either party gives at least 90 days' notice before the end of the current period.
The Supplier may suspend access to the Platform if any undisputed Subscription Fees remain unpaid for more than 30 days after the due date.
On termination, the Supplier shall make the Customer Data available for export for 30 days, after which it may delete it.
Liability and law
The Supplier's aggregate liability in each contract year shall not exceed the Subscription Fees paid in that year.
These Terms are governed by the law of England and Wales.

This Agreement is dated 14 July 2025 and is made between Larkspur Retail Group plc of 20 Mill Lane, Bristol BS1 4XY (the "Client") and Tessellate Data Consulting Ltd of 5 Quay Street, Leeds LS2 7AB (the "Consultant").
The Services
Scope
The Consultant shall provide the data migration and reporting services described in Schedule 1 (the "Services") from the Commencement Date until the end of the Term.
Standard of performance
The Consultant shall perform the Services with reasonable skill and care, in accordance with good industry practice and in compliance with all applicable laws, including the Data Protection Act 2018.
Client obligations
The Client shall provide the Consultant with access to its premises, systems and personnel as reasonably required for the performance of the Services.
Fees and payment
Rates
The Client shall pay the Consultant for each day on which the Services are performed at the rates in the table below, together with any reasonable expenses approved in advance by the Client.
Role
Day rate
Maximum days
Lead consultant
Data engineer
Invoicing
The Consultant shall invoice the Client monthly in arrears, and the Client shall pay each valid invoice within 30 days of receipt.

If the Client fails to pay any amount by the due date, the Consultant may charge interest under the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998 at the rate of 4% per year above the Bank of England base rate.
Intellectual property

All intellectual property rights in the deliverables created by the Consultant in performing the Services shall vest in the Client on creation, and the Consultant hereby assigns those rights to the Client.
Insurance and liability
The Consultant shall maintain professional indemnity insurance with a limit of not less than [●] for each claim throughout the Term and for 6 years afterwards.
Neither party's total liability under this Agreement shall exceed an amount equal to the fees paid in the 12 months before the event giving rise to the claim.
Nothing in this Agreement limits either party's liability for:
death or personal injury caused by its negligence;
fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation; or
any other liability which cannot be limited by law.
Business Continuity

If any provision of this Agreement is found to be invalid or unenforceable, that provision shall be deemed modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid, and the remaining provisions shall not be affected.
Termination
Either party may terminate this Agreement by giving not less than 60 days' written notice to the other party.
Either party may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect if the other party commits a material breach which is not remedied within 14 days of a written request to do so.

On termination under clause 6.1 or clause 6.2, the Client shall pay the Consultant for all Services performed up to the date of termination, and the Consultant shall return all property of the Client in its possession.
General
The Consultant is an independent contractor and nothing in this Agreement creates a relationship of employment, partnership or agency between the parties.
This Agreement is governed by the law of England and Wales.

new: Side Letter
In relation to the shareholders' agreement of Orbital Kitchen Ltd
To: Priya Fernando, Founder
Dear Priya,

We refer to the shareholders' agreement dated [DATE] between Orbital Kitchen Ltd (the "Company") and its shareholders (the "Shareholders' Agreement"). Terms defined in the Shareholders' Agreement have the same meaning in this letter.
The Company confirms that the Founder shall be entitled to appoint one director to the Board for so long as she holds at least 10% of the Shares in issue.
The Founder shall be a Good Leaver if she ceases to be an employee by reason of death, serious ill health or permanent disability, or if she is dismissed without Cause.
The Founder shall be a Bad Leaver if her employment is terminated by the Company for Cause, or if she resigns within 24 months of the date of the Shareholders' Agreement.
If the Founder is a Bad Leaver, she shall be required to transfer all of her Shares at the lower of their nominal value and their fair market value.
If the Founder is a Good Leaver, she shall be required to transfer only her Unvested Shares, at their fair market value.
The Shares held by the Founder shall vest in accordance with the schedule below, subject to a cliff of 12 months.
Vesting date
Shares vesting
First anniversary
Second anniversary
Third anniversary
The investors agree that the Founder may transfer up to 5% of her Shares to a family trust, provided that the trustees first sign a deed of adherence.
This letter is supplemental to the Shareholders' Agreement, and in the event of every conflict between them, this letter shall prevail.
This letter shall terminate automatically on the earlier of an Exit and the date on which the Founder ceases to hold any Shares.
This letter is governed by the law of England and Wales.
Yours sincerely,
For and on behalf of Orbital Kitchen Ltd.
